elements.content: Grammar focus: Cleft Sentences and Emphasis.

Pick the element the reader must remember, then put it in the focus slot: after it was for the it-cleft, at the end for the what-cleft. Watch the agreement in the what-cleft, where what is singular even when the complement is plural.

it-cleft — focus after it was: it was the delay that cost us the contract
what-cleft — focus at the end: what cost us the contract was the delay
negative cleft — focus on what is not the cause: it is not the cost that worries me
all-cleft — focus on the only thing: all I asked for was a decision
there-cleft — presents an entity: there was a delay that cost us the contract
cleft with a time or place — highlights an adverbial: it was in June that the policy changed
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: '___ we need is more time.'
2. Complete: 'It was the supplier ___ missed the deadline.'
3. Which sentence corrects an assumption?
options: It wasn't the cost that stopped us; it was the timing.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

It was the board that rejected the plan. — The board rejected the plan. (It-cleft: highlights the board.)
What the board rejected was the plan. — The board rejected the plan. (What-cleft: highlights the plan.)
It was in June that the policy changed. — The policy changed in June. (Highlights a time.)
What do you observe?

A cleft splits one sentence into two clauses so that the highlighted element sits in its own slot. The it-cleft opens with it was and places the focus after it: it was the delay that cost us the contract. The what-cleft opens with what and places the focus at the end: what cost us the contract was the delay. Both keep the original meaning and change only the emphasis.
1. Which cleft puts the focus at the end of the sentence?
2. Does a cleft change the meaning of a sentence?
options: Yes, it negates part of it.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: Can critique cultural exhibitions and express aesthetic judgments using cleft sentences for emphasis

Success criteria:
- I can highlight a subject with an it-cleft.
- I can highlight an object with a what-cleft.
- I can keep the agreement right in a what-cleft.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ What we need are a clear owner (agreement with a plural complement) → ✅ What we need is a clear owner
❌ It was the delay what cost us the contract (what after an it-cleft) → ✅ It was the delay that cost us the contract
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

It wasn't the price that lost the deal, it was the delivery date.
All the board asked for was a timetable.
It was in March that the first warning appeared.
